fact: ONECI's director general said the national civil-status management system is deployed in 699 civil-registry centres and over four million civil-status records are digitised, and 283 digital birth-registration terminals were handed to health workers in Tonkpi for progressive rollout.

fact: AIP reports ONECI equipped all civil-registry centres of mairies and sous-préfectures at the end of 2025 with computer equipment and the Citiweb software for digital registration of births, marriages and deaths.
AIP reports the Citiweb software deployed in all mairie and sous-préfecture civil-registry centres is for digital registration of births, marriages, deaths and other acts.

AIP reports ONECI deployed the Citiweb software in the mairies and sous-préfectures of the Gôh region, with all centres equipped at the end of 2025 and agent training under way since then, 44 agents trained in Gagnoa from 27 July 2026.
AIP reports the Citiweb software deployed by ONECI captures births, marriages and deaths in all mairie and sous-préfecture centres, equipped at the end of 2025.

ONECI's project head said birth data will be recorded in health centres via terminals connected to the national civil-status software, first tests in Abidjan were conclusive, and rollout nationwide is to follow.
ONECI's director general said digitisation of civil status is effective, with 98% of civil-registry centres computerised and connected to the Cityweb software.

ONECI's director general said on 16 September 2025 that ONECI covers more than 84% of civil-status centres with a digital civil-status system linked to a national server, which is linked to the Registre national des personnes physiques.

ONECI deputy director general Pélagie Gonto said in October 2024 that the Cityweb software is deployed in 434 civil registration centres (303 sub-prefectures and 131 communes), a deployment rate of 62.89%, and that digitisation of civil status registers was piloted at 100% in the Grand-Bassam town hall.
ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 list under digitalisation the digitisation of civil status registers and a gradual move from paper to digital, with 692 civil registration centres in the country.

ONECI's CityWeb web application, which records birth, marriage and death acts, is deployed in several regions and town halls, with 5,453 acts at Abobo in September 2026 and up to 62.5% of centres inactive in Moronou.
CityWeb lets registrars create, process and follow birth, marriage and death acts, according to the ONECI account reported by Digital Mag.
